D: A mouse detective in 1897 London takes on Professor Ratigan to rescue a kidnapped toymaker.
P: Serve the snacks when Mrs Judson brings in the cheese crumpets.
S: Mrs Judson's cheese crumpets at Baker Street
Crumpets toasted, spread with butter and topped with grated cheddar and a little mustard, grilled until bubbling.
Scotch eggs of soft-boiled eggs wrapped in pork sausage meat, crumbed and fried, with mustard.

Gingerbread cut into toy shapes, baked at 180C for 10 minutes, piped with white icing. Melt 125g butter, 100g brown sugar and 125ml golden syrup together. Sift 375g plain flour with 1 tsp bicarb, 3 tsp ground ginger and 1 tsp cinnamon, then stir in the butter mix and 1 beaten egg. Knead into a dough and chill 30 minutes. Roll to 5mm and cut into toy soldiers, teddies and tops. Bake on lined trays at 180C for 10 minutes. Cool, then pipe with icing of 150g icing sugar and a little egg white.
M: Lamb mince with onion, carrot and peas under buttery mash, baked at 200C until golden.

Beef topside roasted at 200C to medium, rested, with Yorkshire puddings, roast potatoes and gravy made from the pan. Rub a 1.5kg beef topside with oil, salt and mustard powder and roast at 200C for 50 minutes for medium. Rest 15 minutes. Roast 1kg parboiled potatoes in hot oil for 50 minutes. Whisk 140g plain flour, 4 eggs and 200ml milk. Heat oil in a 12-hole muffin tin at 230C, pour in the batter and bake 20 minutes without opening the door. Stir 1 tbsp flour into the pan juices, add 300ml beef stock and simmer into gravy.
W: Two vanilla sponges baked at 180C for 25 minutes, sandwiched with strawberry jam and whipped cream, dusted with icing sugar.
K: Basil and Dawson's rooms at Baker Street

Earl Grey brewed strong and chilled with lemon juice and honey, topped with sparkling water over ice and served with a shortbread finger. Steep 4 Earl Grey tea bags in 600ml boiling water for 5 minutes, remove and stir in 3 tbsp honey. Chill for 2 hours. Add the juice of 3 lemons. Fill 4 glasses with ice and lemon slices, pour in the tea to two thirds full and top with 300ml sparkling water. Serve with shortbread fingers.

s.note: Mrs Judson's cheese crumpets at Baker Street
s.how: Toast 8 crumpets until golden and spread with butter. Mix 200g grated cheddar with a spoon of English mustard and pile onto each crumpet. Grill until bubbling and golden. Serve hot on a plate for a hungry detective.

Boil 4 eggs for 6 minutes, cool and peel. Wrap each in 100g pork sausage mince. Roll in flour, beaten egg and panko, then fry at 170C for 6 minutes until golden. Halve and serve with English mustard, like a bar snack in a dodgy pub.

m.how: Brown 800g lamb mince with a diced onion and 2 grated carrots. Add a cup of peas and a little water and simmer for 30 minutes until thick. Spread in a dish, top with mash from 1kg potatoes and plenty of butter and bake at 200C until golden.

w.how: Beat 200g butter with 200g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 200g self-raising flour. Bake in 2 tins at 180C for 25 minutes. Cool, then sandwich with strawberry jam and whipped cream. Dust the top with icing sugar and serve at half past four.

d.note: Basil and Dawson's rooms at Baker Street
d.how: Steep 4 Earl Grey tea bags in 600ml boiling water for 5 minutes, remove and stir in 3 tbsp honey. Chill for 2 hours. Add the juice of 3 lemons. Fill 4 glasses with ice and lemon slices, pour in the tea to two thirds full and top with 300ml sparkling water. Serve with shortbread fingers.
